title: Dragon Quest IX: Sentinels of the Starry Skies
subtitle: A guardian among mortals

body: Dragon Quest IX: Sentinels of the Starry Skies is Level-5 and Square Enix's Nintendo DS role-playing adventure about a Celestrian stranded in the mortal world. The player creates this fallen guardian and the companions who travel alongside them. Towns, monsters and quests retain the series' approachable fantasy style, but local multiplayer lets friends enter the journey together. The personalised party gives the adventure a different emphasis from following a fixed cast. Its heroes can look like the player's own group, preparing for the same discoveries and battles.

Monsters are visible while exploring, so an encounter begins when the party makes contact rather than arriving only as an unseen interruption. Battles use familiar turn-based commands for attacks, abilities, spells, items and defence. The player can direct each companion or assign automated tactics. Creating the other party members makes their preparation part of the same process as designing the protagonist. A balanced group needs more than a distinctive appearance: equipment, available abilities and the role of each traveller determine what happens when a visible threat finally catches them.

Optional quests and an alchemy system provide reasons to gather ingredients, inspect treasure and keep playing beyond the next story destination. The handheld format also supports local communication, including the exchange of treasure maps through its anonymous communication mode. That feature made carrying the game through a crowded place part of its appeal in Japan. Dragon Quest IX connects the long, private routines of a role-playing adventure with the possibility of encountering somebody else's progress, allowing a portable machine to carry both a party and an invitation.
